nahr-al-ishq-wa-bahr-al-gharam.title: The River of Passion and the Sea of Love
nahr-al-ishq-wa-bahr-al-gharam.d1: “The River of Passion and the Sea of Love” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
nahr-al-ishq-wa-bahr-al-gharam.d2: From the king of passion and fidelity, king of the heart and all it holds
desc: As I surrender my heart to this ink, I do not hope to speak as a lecturer mounting the pulpits of learning, nor as a teacher drilling lessons in the shade of books, but as a lover whose wounds have opened onto the light of the phrase, and whose depths have burst forth as the dawn bursts with the first thread of morning light. I am here to give voice to fires that cannot be spoken in the clamour of life, and to bring out treasures that are measured not in gold or silver but in a glow that flows through the veins, and in meanings that set the breast of time alight.

The pen in my hand is not a tool that records, but an ember that speaks, a heart that beats, a spring that opens at the edges of the inner self. I do not address minds alone; I carve my words on the strings of the soul. Love here is not an ornament of metaphor, nor a picture hung on a wall, but a light that breaks in on us, an overflowing that lifts us, a tremor that carries a person from his earth to his horizon. And passion is not a feather for speech or a showpiece for poetry, but the scale of the heart when it trembles, the touchstone of love when it blazes, and a light by which a person’s sincerity in giving and sacrifice is tested. It is a key that opens the doors of the soul onto its secret, a mirror that reveals a self we thought was hidden, and a river that runs in our depths to remind us that life is not built on bread alone, but on the ember of love when it glows, and on the cry of passion when it wakes.

Whoever has tasted passion has come to know himself, and whoever has been kept from it has lost half the truth. It is the light that completes what we lack and the flame that raises us. No heart touched by love but opens like a rose drenched in the dew of dawn, and no soul flooded by passion but rises like the wing of a bird soaring towards a sky beyond reach. It is a spring that quenches the thirst of dreams, a brand that lights the road, a song the inner self wakes to every dawn, until love seems to be what opens a door within that giving never closes, and raises us to a station reached only by those who have burned in its light. Love is what plucks loneliness from the nerves of time and shapes it into companionship, and silences the hush of life until it becomes a song the depths repeat as if learning to fly. It makes of every wound a balcony overlooking a light deeper than eyes can see; it gathers what was scattered of our selves as the winds gather the clouds just before rain; and it wakes in us what had gone out, like a lamp that returns to shine after years of stillness.

In the pages of a lifetime, love writes lines that last, as if they were not ink but a moment of insight revealing the road our steps had lost. Through passion a person becomes more beautiful, not because he has grown handsome, but because he feels that his existence has a glow and a voice. Through love the world softens like a stone warmed by the glow of dawn, and life rises as if in a new upwelling that sets its pulse in order again. Love is a light that splits the darkness until its night is ended; seeds that rise in the belly of the earth in colours the expanses of space cannot teach and the bounds of distance cannot contain; and a bridge that binds person to person even when continents and distances lie between them. Through love the houses of the soul are rebuilt after the winds have drained them; through passion ears of grain are sown in the plains of the inner self and grow on the edges of hearts; and through love the world widens even when it has closed in, and doors open that had seemed like rock.

Love is not a passing accident but a covenant carved in the bone before the heart, a pledge the soul ratifies before tongues proclaim it. With it, life becomes a green land that does not wither, and in its light hearts remain dwellings of happiness, strongholds of affection and anchors of joy. It is the light of meaning and the secret of beauty: it bursts like a spring in a person’s depths and waters him, and falls like a cloud on the deserts within, so that their fields flower in colours of laughter and hope. It is a gleam that guides through the mazes of the roads, and the voice of passion that gives the heart back its beat after a silence that weighed on it. Through love every tear turns into a pearl that lights the night of weeping, and every moan into a melody that opens the gates of hope; through it ears of affection are planted in hearts and grow with the days like the harvest of love in a field of light.

Love is a secret speech passed between the eyes before the tongue, a promise written in the pages of a lifetime before events confirm it, and a flash of lightning that reveals a person’s worth to himself. No heart opened its door to love but breathed freedom, and no soul drank from the spring of passion but came back purer and richer. It is the journey in which the soul ascends, the key that leads to the deepest doors of the heart, and the proof that a person is not complete without a love that dwells in him and lifts him to a horizon reached only by those who have burned in its light. Passion is not a word said and then gone, nor a thought recalled and then extinguished, but a hymn renewed each time the dawn rises, and a truth that remains each time life is renewed. Every day it is born, in every inner self it grows, and in every heart it writes its text and sets down its mark like a lasting inheritance.

As I take leave of these words, I see love as a covenant for the inner self, a testament for existence, and a bridge between one person and another. It is the light that does not go out and the song that does not fall silent: a full moon lighting the way for travellers, a candle guiding the lost, and a rain that makes the paths of the bewildered bloom. Whoever has not found a road in love has lost the way, and whoever has not found a homeland in passion has lost half of tranquillity. If history has books that record the deeds of kings, love has ledgers more splendid and more radiant, in which the dreams of lovers are written and the names of those who believed that existence flourishes only through a heart beating with affection shine. This book is not a page turned over in the hands, nor a manuscript folded away in the corners of forgetting; it is a key to those ledgers, a bridge to those roads, and a breath from a river that has run in hearts since the first day a human being loved, and will run until the last heart that beats with passion.

Love is not a metaphor sailing the sea of poetry, nor a simile that writers hang on the walls of their phrases, nor a pun in which the word plays tricks, hiding one meaning and showing another, nor a metonymy that hides behind sayings and then shows its secret, nor an antithesis in which light stands beside darkness, nor a parallel that balances the force of pain against the radiance of hope, nor a metaphor that moves the sun into the palms or settles the moon in the eyes, nor rhymed prose singing in the ear of time, nor a double meaning playing between a surface that distracts and a depth that reveals, nor a quotation drawing its light from the springs of wisdom. Above all of that, it is a pulse that cannot be erased, a promise that does not fall, and a truth that remains even as the ages change.

It is a crown of existence renewed by its own light, a ship sailing on through the days: if it vanishes from the eye of life, the radiance remains; if its voice is hidden, the faith remains. Love is the right that does not lapse and the promise that does not betray, the strength that kindles the rush of life in the body. Through it the weak becomes a mountain that takes on the winds, the broken a sword that regains its hardness, and the exile a homeland he carries in his breast wherever he goes. It is the strength that gathers what was scattered, binds up what was broken and rebuilds what was torn down; it is an army that raises the human heart onto the platforms of victory, and a key that opens the doors of hearts so that rivers of passion burst forth. No soul swam in its sea but came back pure, and no breast breathed it in but grew wide and open. Love, O owner of a heart, is the strength that sets up within a person a kingdom of resolve, and the voice that calls in his depths and turns his silence into a song.

When passion is absent the building falls apart; when love is present, dreams rise up like armies of light. It is the strength that makes human glory and the key that opens the doors of tomorrow. No heart in which love has made its home but becomes a throne on which wisdom sits, and no soul lit by love but becomes a lamp lighting the way of nations. It is the energy of souls, the breath of life and the covenant of renewal.

When love settles in the heart, it raises a person from his dust to his highest horizon, wakes in him the dignity and courage that had slept, and urges him to rise like one born again on the balconies of light. It is the brand that kindles the beginning, the wind that carries the ship of life to the safety of the shore, and the secret that, once it takes hold of a person’s breast, changes the landmarks of time and goes beyond the bounds of the familiar. Love makes the weak an unconquerable fortress, the broken a sword that regains its splendour, and the bewildered a star by which travellers find their way.

As long as there is a pulse in hearts that says “I love”, there is a power in the world that lengthens hope, gathers what was scattered of life’s fragments, and lays out for a person a path he walks as if walking on a bridge of light, endurance and glory. Love is not a passing state; it is the crown that crowns the human essence, the breath that awakens meanings of strength in the breast, and the harbour where the ship of thought anchors to begin its journey towards a day more beautiful, more at ease and more exalted.

If history has doors through which the deeds of kings enter, love has greater doors that open onto a world of light and meaning. It is the end of selfishness and the rise of humanity; it is reunion after estrangement, affection after loneliness, and peace after war. It is the root that clings in the depths, the branch that rises towards the sky, and the road that gathers souls around the table of existence.

Through passion hope is sown in the breast; through love the houses of the soul are built on pillars of light, and existence becomes a city of calm and peace of mind. Through affection the doors of hearts open and a clarity enters them like gardens of good tidings; through love the stains of the soul fall away and the days are adorned with the pearls of faithfulness; through fondness hearts unite like a pure stream running through the valley of existence; and through feeling the voice of life shimmers, so that every heartbeat sings a song of gentle hope.

Through feeling, silence turns into eloquence and sunset into a shining dawn; through emotion the ceilings of minds are raised and visions of joy dwell beneath them; through the heart’s sense the letter opens its two wings and swims in the space of beauty; through love a person rises to distant heights and becomes himself a stairway of light; through passion existence turns into a melody of splendour, the roads blossom and meanings sing; through rapture every lover becomes a bird borne on the wings of longing towards horizons of tenderness; and through ardour hearts sing and write songs of faithfulness in the pages of time.

Through tenderness harshness softens, the walls of cruelty fall and every wound opens like a flower; through gentleness wounds become melodies and tears become jewels lighting the evening; through closeness roads meet, the distant comes near and the dark comes into bloom; through companionship meeting grows sweet and the days sparkle like pearls on the necklace of the heart; and through longing, yearning trembles in the ears of existence and plays its sweetest tunes.

Through hope the rust is washed from faces and the doors of tomorrow open onto light; through faithfulness the roads are decked with banners of trust and love remains master over hearts; through dreams existence grows larger and becomes gentler, clearer and more splendid; through each breath hearts are fed with the light of tenderness and the branches of giving come into leaf; through the pulse time walks as a song and a lifetime turns into a poem; through desires souls sway and light the lamps of hope along their paths; through sincerity passion becomes clear as water without murk or dust; and through reverence love becomes a crown that adorns hearts and raises them to the seat of dignity.

Through admiration the features light up and the face becomes a garden of splendour; through desire the horizon of closeness opens and every road is carpeted with the flowers of hope; through high resolve love rises to lofty stations and lights up the bounds of life; through yearning the heart trembles like a string singing the night of longing; through burning, longing glows like an ember lighting the roads; through delight love is renewed and souls bloom like an everlasting spring; through joy passion becomes the sweetest of songs and life turns into a season in flower; through ecstasy hearts borrow two wings and soar in the horizon of eloquence; through gladness existence is filled with songs of contentment; and through contentment the story is complete, and love is crowned a king who guides the days in clarity and splendour.

fi-hadrat-al-samt.title: In the Presence of Silence
fi-hadrat-al-samt.sub: A Journey Through the Sea of Meanings and the Mirror of Existence
fi-hadrat-al-samt.d1: “In the Presence of Silence” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
desc: At the beginning of the story, this book was not a project already printed in the mind, nor a title leading a set of pages. It was a question pressing in the depths of the soul: how can a person regain his balance in a world choking on noise and losing its measure with every raised voice?

From there began the search for another space, one not measured by the number of words nor bounded by what speeches and slogans record; a space in which silence steps forward to become a scale for reflection, an appointed time for thought, and a platform on which a person stands before himself before he stands before the world. This is how the idea of “In the Presence of Silence” was born: not as a text arranged in chapters and sections, but as a balance in which the reader is meant to stand at the edge of himself and see how calm can repair what time has spoiled and what voices have scattered.

This book was not the fruit of passing enthusiasm, nor the result of a single moment of inspiration. It took some eight years of toil, scrutiny and close observation of how meaning flows through life and experience. Long years in which the pen rose and fell, writing one page and erasing another, replacing one word with another, lifting one sentence and dropping the next, until the weak words fell away and what remained was worthy of standing in the place of strong, precise expression.

So this book was not shaped in haste, nor did it rely on quick phrasing or loose construction. It was built as fortresses are built: stone upon stone, meaning upon meaning, statement completing statement, until it rested on four pillars: patience that steadies it, knowledge that illuminates it, language that carries it, and a conscience that holds every sentence to account before it settles into place.

“In the Presence of Silence” is not a book seeking a place for itself among the titles on a shelf, nor does it try to compete with the glory of this poet or that writer. It hopes only to stand where language performs its true role: guiding thought, correcting perception, and building a bridge between the inner world and the scenes of reality. That is why this work draws on the strongest tools of the language: eloquent form, rigorous construction, depth of simile, and interwoven images that seek no ornament but fight on the side of meaning to bring out its strength and majesty.

In this book an inner rhythm runs firmly; you hear in it the echo of the old Arabic rhymed prose, but in a new garment that rejects affectation and raises meaning above every verbal flourish that has no support in thought. There the reader feels that he is not merely receiving phrases, but crossing with the word a bridge that carries him from the bank of distraction to the bank of focus, and from scattered attention to the station of disciplined contemplation.

No wonder, then, that after these years of work this book is closer to a raised edifice of language than to a volume folded away on a back shelf. It addresses a person’s mind, converses with his heart, speaks to his historical memory, and calls up in him what he has learned from the dictionaries of the language and the springs of authentic Arabic expression. Yet for all that, it does not claim perfection; it invites the reader to continue the journey: the journey of a silence that preserves the dignity of the word, of a dialogue not spoiled by barren argument, and of a reading that refuses to be a quick pass over the lines and wants instead to be an honest encounter with the self and the world around it. This is the author’s word to whoever opens this book: do not read it as hurried pages are read. Enter with it into the presence of silence, and let your thought climb its steps as one climbs a mountain, step after step, until it reaches the summit from which things are seen as they ought to be seen, not as one has been made to see them.

These pages are not the end of a road but the key to another beginning. I gathered in them what silence inspired in my heart, not to be the owner of a voice that rises and then dies down, nor to wear them as an ornament in gatherings of empty claims, but to offer an open covenant, a bequest of insight, and a key for anyone who wishes to open the door of his soul onto a wider light, to breathe the meanings of truth with deeper sincerity, and to see in silence a ladder to the realm of knowledge. In every letter there is a pulse of wisdom running through the arteries of reflection, so the reader sees what lies behind the word and witnesses between its lines a radiance that sings the breath of light and composes the melodies of knowledge.

They are a breeze of thought and awareness, an echo of light moving between stillness and radiance. They refresh the heart, nurture in it the meaning of serenity, and reveal to it the places of hidden beauty that are not seen with the eye but felt by the heart and grasped by thought. With every sentence the reader walks as if through a garden of light, arranging its meanings like flowers in winds of calm and dignity.

I wrote this book as a journey with the self before it was a journey with the pen; a journey in which I sat with my silence, listened to the whisper of my time, and conversed with the echo of my days. I found no truer scale than silence, no fairer judge, and no wider school. It is the mirror that shows what is hidden, the field in which thought grows, and the door that opens onto knowledge, revealing to the soul the secret of its slumber and the seeds of its light. I did not intend to list ordered meanings or collect scattered sayings; I intended to offer an experience I lived, a truth I touched, and a key whose power I believe in. I hand you, dear reader, a key: use it well and it will open new doors for you; leave it by the road and it remains useless iron. A book does not work in your place or think instead of you; it is a travelling companion, a mirror for reflection, and a scale on which your steps are weighed.

I know that an honest word may stir argument, kindle debate and lift veils that falsehood had kept in place, and that it may shake thrones built on illusion and greed. Wherever truth speaks, the palaces of falsehood tremble and the hearts of those who hate the light are unsettled. And yet that is the word’s true place and highest mission: to stir thought from its slumber, wake minds from their heedlessness, and rouse consciences from the intoxication of habit and the calm of conformity.

A word that moves no feeling, raises no question and leaves no trace is nothing but a cold breath in the air of heedlessness. And a silence that grows no insight and yields no wisdom is the stillness of death in the garment of life: it looks calm, but within it the spirits are extinguished. Blessed is a word that tells the truth even if it hurts, and a silence that grows light even if it saddens; for in the shaking of thought truths are born, and in the stillness of wisdom the light of existence appears.

Dear reader, I do not ask you for blind following or mute repetition. I invite you to a dialogue that raises your inner balance and awakens in you the light of insight, whose call is heard only by pure hearts. This book is not a minaret from which opinion is recited, nor a pulpit from which convictions are dictated; it is a mirror that shows every reader what he hides within himself, if he looks into it honestly. Whatever agrees with you, keep it and act on it, for it is the growth of your own wisdom; and whatever differs from you, debate it with insight and a steady mind. Dialogue is the breath of thought and the soul of life.

The aim of this path is not to make you a shadow resembling me, but to give back to you the voice that the voices of the crowd made you lose, and to revive in you the thought that the clamour of life made you neglect, so that you return to yourself as clear as you were created and see the truth with the eye of your own heart, not through the microscope of others. If this path touches your heart with warmth, raises a question in you, or opens before you a door into the depths of your soul, then that is what I seek. A word that kindles no thought does not deserve to be written, and a thought that shakes no stillness is no thought at all.

The word is an ember that ignites, and silence is a spring that leads somewhere; in the harmony between them insight is born, guiding hearts and baptising minds. This book is not pages to be read but a journey to be lived. Its words stir the rubble in the depths of a person and remind him that knowledge is not given without effort and is drawn out only through contemplation and patience. So shake off the dust of silence, open the window of the soul onto a brighter light, and listen to the voice of the word as it travels through the kingdoms of thought like a breeze glorifying God in the light. In the word there is life, in silence there is radiance, and between them the new human being climbs the ladder of wisdom towards a light that does not fade. Success comes from God, and in Him is our trust. And these are my last words to you, in verse rather than prose… in the presence of silence:
My silence is my weapon in this life, and my banner;
in it the truth unveils its face, relied upon.
I have woven wisdom onto the letters, and it appeared
as a light that chants an appointed promise in the minds that see.
Whoever comes to read what I have written, meanings
burst forth in him, and he wakes up ablaze.
These words of mine came to me from my silence,
a breath that lights the soul and steadies the mind.
With the wisdom of the physician in their ordering
I brought words to life, precise as medicine.
And with the writer’s pen I traced experiences
through which hearts ask the stars for their glow.
In every verse there is strength and firmness
that shakes the age and wakes glory to greater glory.
In my silence I sank into a sea of knowledge,
and saw in its depths a meaning all its own.
For silence is the legacy of life and its secret,
standing firm through the passing of time.
And by my pen maturity remains a lighthouse
that guides minds and makes the right path clear.

From here your first step into meaning begins, neither as a follower nor as one led, but as a witness to yourself and a questioner of your own vision. If you find a mirror in these words, look into it long; and if you find a road in them, walk it with awareness. Wisdom does not give itself to those who hurry it, but to those who walk towards it with a wakeful heart.

ala-jidar-al-zaman.title: On the Wall of Time
ala-jidar-al-zaman.d1: “On the Wall of Time” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
desc: I do not claim that these pages will save the world, nor that they will mend what years have spoiled. But I believe, and belief is a measure, that a word which is true creates, a word which is pure uplifts, and a word which stands straight rebuilds in the soul what has collapsed of the house of meaning. Many books are good at adorning and poor at explaining; they raise the voice and drop the evidence; they dazzle the moment and impoverish the outcome. This book does not want to be an ornament on the shelves; its aim is to be a mirror within, because the gravest thing that afflicts us is not a shortage of time but a shortage of meaning, not narrow living but narrow vision.

If “On the Wall of Time” is a title, it is also a pledge: to speak of what lasts, not of what passes; of what steadies a person, not of what intoxicates him; of what raises value, not of what raises noise. This book was written because I saw, in people’s lives, their gatherings and their experiences, that many of us hurry along the road yet lag in maturity; advance in age yet lag in understanding; grow wide in information yet narrow in wisdom. I saw that time had become a stage demanding constant performance from us, and that society sometimes wants an image rather than a life story, an appearance rather than a substance, a title rather than a course to run. So I said: why not return the human being to his rightful place? Why not make depth the measure instead of glitter? Why not restore to values their authority and to awareness its standing? I do not lecture the reader, nor do I look down on him; we are all seekers of meaning, all busy mending an inner self that sometimes shatters in the clamour outside.

Hence this work: not as preaching to be consumed, but as dialogue to be cultivated; not as ornate wording, but as the building of meaning; not as the arranging of sentences, but as the ordering of a soul. The method of this book is to draw out of life what it hides while it shows, and to call things by their names, without a softening that weakens the truth or an embellishment that corrupts insight. I will speak to you of time as a test of substance, of disagreement as a training of character, and of the small details that form a personality as drops form the course of a river. I will pursue shallowness with depth, and hold to a single idea: that a person is built by accumulation, torn down by laxity, raised by consistency, and brought low by double standards.

I do not like a style that lulls the reader with sedatives; I prefer a style that wakes him with things witnessed: a style with ring, not racket; with rhyme, not affectation; with a beauty that serves meaning and does not veil it. If you find sharpness in some lines, it is the sharpness of clarity, not the harshness of judgement; if you find strictness, it is the strictness of the scale, not a cramping of the spirit; if you find art, it is art harnessed for building, not for display. And you, reader, are not a listener in the back row but a partner in meaning. This book does not ask you for applause but for attention; it does not court admiration but rouses awareness; it does not promise you easy pleasure but points you to a demanding dignity. You will find in it that a person grows not by what he obtains but by what he manages to preserve of himself: his balance, his poise, and his faith that values are neither bought nor sold. If time has a wall, the noblest thing carved on it is not a name on a sign but character in a life; not a voice blaring from a loudspeaker but a mark left on a soul; not a clamour that rises and dies down but a meaning that takes root and then spreads.

If you come out of these pages more aware of yourself, more careful of your balance, and more protective of what humanity deserves from you, then together we will have set one true letter on the wall of time, and in the reckoning of meaning that is greater than all noise and more lasting than all glitter.

Now that you have read this word, know that I did not write it to decorate the entrance of the book, but to hand you its key and its lamp. Books are like houses: some have a shining door and little room inside, and some are spacious within and modest without. This book does not borrow a glare to captivate the reader, nor beg for astonishment to hide poverty of thought; it draws its strength from people’s conduct when the lights go out and only consciences remain, and from their lives when the applauders fall silent and the deeds speak. If you are looking for a text that sweetens the truths for you and fattens your illusions, look elsewhere; and if you want a voice that flatters heedlessness and makes peace with contradiction, I am not its companion. This book is like a scalpel: not to wound but to heal; and like a mirror: not to make ugly but to make you see. In it I will offer you the knowledge of meaning in the arena of life, the understanding of the soul in the trials of the days, and the refining of character in the face of chaos, so that you know refinement is not an ornament to be hung but a structure to be built, and that depth is not obscurity to be traded on but clarity to be defended.

You will see that I do not set meanings on air or build lines on sand. A saying not backed by experience becomes froth, and thought not joined to conduct becomes play. In this book I will redefine strength: not shouting that overpowers, but steadfastness that prevails; not severity that frightens, but wisdom that refines; not hardness that smashes, but soundness that repairs. I will show you how time lures us into exchanging principles for interests, values for rules, and a life story for an image; then I will show you how value is recovered from the jaws of noise, and how meaning is rescued from the siege of speed. I will converse with what in you stays silent while you speak, and with what you ignore while you reason. The mind has its questions, the conscience its arguments, the soul its pitfalls; I neither make light of one nor flatter another. I want a reader who walks the road with me, not one who watches me from the pavement of admiration. This book is a path, not a stage; a building, not an ornament; a pledge, not a passing thought. Perhaps you will ask: what work is this that seeks to weigh morals and sound the depths? I say: it is a constitution that knows words slip away when they are not held firm, and meanings become distorted when they are not served.

In this book I will make language a disciplined sword, not an unruly cleaver; a measured melody, not a scattered din. For me, rhymed prose is architecture that, when sound, strengthens the building; wordplay is an ornament that, when honest, reveals the fine edge of difference; antithesis is a watchtower that exposes contradiction when it dresses itself as agreement. I will defend eloquence not through arrogance but by siding with what is right; I will fight shallowness not with anger but with clear expression; I will combat falsehood not with insult but with argument. The field of speech has grown crowded with pretenders and empty of those who do it well, and I want to be among the few who know how to speak well and how to keep silent about what is unfitting. If it is the nature of this age to make light of the great and belittle the deep, I want to restore the order of values: there is no greatness with lying, no depth with confusion, no gravity with affectation. As for the challenge you seek, it is not one of vanity or boasting. Al-Mutanabbi stood on a summit for its people and spoke in the tongue of his age, and so made the ages hear. But every time has its field and every battle its weapon: if his weapon was poetry that smelts meanings in moulds of fire, mine is prose that polishes thought in a space of light; and if he struck with a line of verse, I try to build with a chapter.

The challenge of this book is to let the reader see himself without adornment, hear his conscience without noise, and stand before his own scale without a lawyer. Whoever accepts this test has entered the field with us. In these pages you will find that beauty does not contradict truthfulness, that depth does not oppose clarity, and that strength needs no shouting to prove itself. If speech is a racecourse, meaning is its horse; if wording is a cloak, character is its body; and this book accepts neither a cloak without a body nor a horse without a racecourse.

So come, let us name things as they are, put each word in its place, and raise the human being to his worth. What remains on the wall of time is not what we say at the beginning but what we are at the end. As the pages go on, you will discover that this book does not address your eyes alone but your insight; it does not stop at the surface of thought but reaches its core. It seeks to free meaning from the shackle of speed, to rescue value from the crowd of images, and to restore balance to a scale whose weight has tipped between appearance and substance.

Not everything prominent is great, nor everything silent weak, nor everything that shines useful. Often firmness lies hidden in calm, weight shows itself in stillness, and truth speaks when pretence falls silent. On this journey I am not betting on quick admiration but on a lasting influence. I do not want an echo that rises and then dies down, but a mark that takes root and then spreads. For me, a word that does not set up a scale in the soul is superfluous; one that does not light insight in the mind is fleeting; and one that does not mend a flaw in vision is ornament without value. That is why this book moves forward with steps that are calm but firm, with phrases that are weighty but controlled, and with a style that unites beauty and seriousness, gentleness and gravity, until a book takes shape that does not affect depth but breathes it, and does not feign majesty but dwells in it. At this point reading becomes an encounter between the reader and himself, between thought and its scale. The pages turn into mirrors, and the phrases into measures that reveal how truly what is said matches what is lived. The aim is not that the reader gains more information but more insight; not that he memorises sentences but that he sets up a scale. Once this understanding settles, the book becomes a lasting intellectual mark, an inner standard, and a flame of awareness that stays alight after the words have faded and the echoes have stilled.

nahnu-asl-al-hikaya.title: We Are the Origin of the Story
nahnu-asl-al-hikaya.sub: The Land Answers Its People in Measure of What They Give
nahnu-asl-al-hikaya.d1: “We Are the Origin of the Story” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
desc: What this book carries is not just words lined up on rows of paper. It is the pulse of a nation that refused to be buried in the ashes, and the voice of a people who wrote their history in blood and pride. It is the breath of the land when it speaks, and the echo of Jerusalem when it cries out in the hearts of its descendants; and when the wounds fall silent, it remains the caller whose voice never fades.

Here the stones speak, and the wounded rises from his wound to write in his own hand and draw from his blood a covenant that will not shatter. Here the book becomes a mother’s cry over the ruins of her home, the song of a child whose laughter was stolen, and the promise of a young man who was never defeated, even when he was absent from the field of the call. In its meanings dignity shines, in its words awareness rises, and in its pages lies a steadfastness that does not waver.

This book is an uprising of the letter and the awareness of a cause, an oath renewed in every heart: that the word born of pain will not be erased by a sword, nor bought at the tables of politics, nor sold in the markets of submission. It is the tent of meaning in the desert of falsification, the fortress of the cause in an age of empty bidding, the voice of the farmer who sowed with one hand and carried a rifle with the other, and the cry of the steadfast guardian whose forehead never neglected prostration.

So do not take its lines lightly. In them are absent faces and erased names, yet they are present in every pulse and every echo. Even if eyes overlook us, and causes come to be traded at the tables of buying and selling, this book remains an argument that does not wear out, and a voice that only extinction can silence.

Open this book and look between its lines: you will see that we never accepted silence, never moved away from a right, and never exchanged the wound for a bond that would strip the homeland of its meaning. We kept guarding the word, protecting awareness and planting history with pens that do not tremble. This book is not the end of the story, nor a tale to be folded away; it is the torch that carries the light to those who come after, and writes for every generation a line that carries its rescue and raises its honour.

And if they ask one day, “Who are you?”, let this book answer for us, and let all its lines be voices declaring that we were never a footnote in the scenes of history, nor a shadow in the stories of nations; we were the pulse, the wounds, the oath, and the word that refused to fall in the battles of silence.

This book does not decorate paper with suspended dreams, nor make ornaments without substance. It reveals to every reader the awareness of a nation that went through more than can be told, endured what cannot be written, and refused to sell its voice in the markets of submission.

When time passes over its pages and the winds of denial try to erase its letters, they will remain as if carved on a mountain, undefeated by the storms of forgery and unbroken by conspiracies of erasure and concealment. Here the homeland writes in its own hand, and here we prove that we are stronger than erasure and deeper than forgetting, and that our voice, however much ears close to it, will remain a light in the sky of truth whose rays do not set.
We are the mountains; in us the homeland takes root,
and on us the eyes rest through the passing of history.
The right does not fall while there is resolve in us,
even if madness follows madness through our nights.
We walk the road, unafraid of its storms;
the wind kneels when our branches rise high.
This is our book, a voice that calls to us,
in which the truths and the histories become clear.
We are the story; in our depths lives an age
in which glory takes pride, and the free celebrate.

As we open the cover onto these pages, we are not merely announcing a beginning; we are taking up a key to a wider horizon, and setting for the story its direction, one that guides our steps towards meanings deeper than numbering and titles. The story, in its essence, is greater than two brackets that open and close, and greater than paper folded and put away on a distant shelf. It is a continuous journey shaped by honest testimony, careful scrutiny and purity of purpose. Here we write as the steadfast guardian writes his will on the blade of a sword, and we set each letter in its place like the stones of a building destined to last; not for an ornament that dazzles the eye and then fades, but for a truth that speaks to hearts and stays in the memory as the echo of the call to prayer stays with a dawn that always returns. These letters are keys to doors not yet opened, and the torch of a long road that lights the ways and distances still to come.

We proceed through this volume on a line of careful verification and sober precision. A letter that slips misleads, a word that falters darkens, and a vowel mark out of place turns the meaning from its direction. That is why we made this book a balance in which words are weighed as gold dust is weighed on a fine scale: polishing only makes it purer, and revision only removes its impurities. We fix every meaning in its place and give every idea its rightful seat, so that the speech comes out solid as a wall guarding a city, and firm as a mountain that holds back the storms. We weigh our words to match our intentions, so that no glittering metaphor lures us away from a true report, and no ornament of style covers the justice of a proof.

The aim is not merely to shape words, but to establish a direction for the truth, a scale for meanings, and a heartbeat that does not stop. When truth loses its direction it is lost; when the word loses its honesty it dies; and when a nation loses its memory it becomes like a ship tossing in a dark sea. We write to prove that the story is not extinguished but is born again and again in every free heart and every eye that refuses humiliation. We write to revive a covenant handed down through the generations, and to root values that no years can undo and no winds can block. A book, in its essence, is a covenant read with the heart before the eye, and the key to a door that the children open whenever darkness closes its eyelids.

Between a beginning and an end, events run like a river cutting through the rock of reality, watering the trees of memory and planting in its soil olive trees that root wisdom and steadfastness. Every line here is one of the breaths of a nation, and every phrase a part of a long covenant that the winds of extinction cannot sweep away.

We are not offering lines to be folded away, but laying a foundation to last, and raising a building that grows taller each time a generation rises to carry the banner and complete the journey. If the book is asked its name, it says: my soul is my name. If asked its time, it says: every moment. And if asked its place, it says: your hearts are my home.

We present this introduction in a melody of eloquence, matched by a rhythm that meets the ear as a drop meets the stone in a stream: it raises no dust and leaves no noise, yet it carves a channel that remains. We arrange the sentences like the strings of an oud, tightened just as much as the melody needs, so that no rhythm falters and no note strays from its purpose. We shape the images like paintings whose colours spread quietly, so that when the eye reaches their end it returns to look for what it missed. This is our promise to the honoured reader: we will not leave the word confused, the meaning vague, or the vowelling unsteady.

This, reader of the heart, is a book opened not to complete a number of pages, but to make up for a lack of insight and raise one’s standing in knowledge. If you find in it something that strengthens your hand, that is the highest aim; and if you find in it something that goes against your desires, then in going against desire lies the life of truth. We ask God, the One who guides and helps, to make this introduction a necklace of light at the head of the reading, and to make what follows clearer in expression and sharper in proof, so that the story runs along the path of truth and the word rises to the station destined for it: to guide, to bear witness, and to last.

The word, my friend, is an arrow that flies true when released from the bow of truth, and a blazing fire when thrown into the pit of falsehood; nothing puts it out but the sea of faith, and nothing veils its light but the clouds of heedlessness. It is a witness written in the pages of history, an echo repeated in the ears of generations, and a banner raised over the battlefields. The word is a trust to be fulfilled, a banner to be carried and a covenant on which the building stands. Whoever carries it without honesty has betrayed it; whoever throws it in the wrong place has misled; whoever makes it a ladder for falsehood has destroyed; and whoever raises it on the support of truth has built, elevated and given life.

If nations are measured by the strength of their swords and the number of their soldiers, this nation is measured by the strength of its word and by how firmly it holds to a truth that does not wear out. Do you not see that the word in its course is like a river in its flow? If it is sweet, it gives life; if it is salt, it brings death.

So it is with letters: if they are pure, they save; if they are murky, they destroy. Here, in these pages, we place the word on a scale as gold is placed on the balance: no tongue stands without proof, and no pen rises without evidence. If eloquence is the key, knowledge is the door; if letters are soldiers, truth is the commander who leads them; and if the word is a banner, justice is the mast on which it stands firm. Truth is measured by the strength of its voice: if it is genuine it lasts, and if it is false it perishes. This is the measure of nations and the path of their survival.

We do not write to satisfy the appetite of a passing reader, nor to decorate walls with ornate words, but to place in every heart a key that opens the door of truth, and to light in every heart a lamp that illuminates the road of justice. A letter is nothing but one of the soldiers of faith, and a word nothing but one of the swords of truth: whoever shapes it with wisdom wins, and whoever wastes it through heedlessness loses. As long as there is breath in our chests, we will carry the word as arrows are carried in battle, never shooting them in vain or releasing them irresponsibly, but setting them on a path that affirms the truth and refutes falsehood. It is a covenant signed by the pen, witnessed by time and affirmed by the hearts of the generations, so that it becomes a mirror for history and a witness to yesterday, today and the days to come.

This book is not a number in a register or a page in a ledger; it is a breath that expands in the chests of nations, and a spirit renewed in times that strive towards the light. It is the cry of truth when falsehood becomes tyrannical, the scale of justice when the scales are overturned, and the song of souls when tongues fall mute. It is a channel for the voice that does not perish, a spring for the truth that does not wither, and proof that the letter, when it is true, becomes more lasting than rock, higher than the peaks, and deeper than a trace in soil that keeps the memory.

It is a painting open on the face of time, crowded with colours and embraced by lines. When you look at it, you see that every line in it is a shining star, every word a seed that grows, and every meaning a mountain raising its head against the winds. It is a notebook of cries and visions, a garden of memory blooming in every season, and a cloud of blessing raining on a land that does not dry. This volume wants only to be a voice for the tormented, a letter for the silent, a statement revealing what history tried to erase, and a light opening in every heart that seeks the truth.

If we are asked, “What is the message of this book?”, we say: it is a flood running through the cracks of time, carrying in its folds silenced voices and tears that eyes shed but history never wrote. And if we are asked, “What is its aim?”, we say: to form in every reader a mirror in which he sees himself, his cause and his destiny. It is like a lamp burning in the darkness, a sword drawn in the face of fear, and a flower that resists in hard rock and grows despite every stone, every rain and every wind.

It is, reader of the heart, the pulse of a nation that will not accept being a faint echo in a forged history, but wants to be an authentic voice in the book of survival. It is a line written in the heart before it is a line on paper, and a covenant in the soul before it is an oath in assemblies. It is a tree whose roots are in the soil of truth and whose branches are in the sky of freedom, and its fruit falls into the hands of the generations as food for memory and provision for the road. Here speech rises from the station of eloquence to the station of rhythm, and poetry sets out to complete what prose began.

So take it, my friend, as a sword is taken in battle: not for decoration but for defence, not for vain pride but for cutting and deciding. Read it as blood is read on the ground: without letters or sound, yet it cries out in the souls. And carry it as a banner is carried: not to be hidden behind curtains, but to be raised above the armies. In its essence it is a call to life, and a declaration that a nation endures as long as there is a voice in it that speaks the truth aloud.
We are those who, when truth calls, answer —
the voice of truth thundering in our hearts.
We are the mountains: when the storms come on,
our steps stand firm, and we make our dwelling there.
Today we lean on nothing but right guidance,
until we clear every folly from the road.
We raise the flag of truth above our heads
until the night withholds its heavy despair.
And we become a light when its darkness thickens,
flowing over the earth as a coming kindness.
This is a book that does not yield to falsehood;
it sends forth its words as a polished sword.
This is a book that does not barter its right;
it proclaims the ancient promise, majestic.
For the truth in us will never be compromised;
it will not pass away, and will never fade.
We build for the voice of truth a firm edifice,
and turn the falsehood of oppression into scattered dust.

dostori.title: My Constitution… A Balance of the Heart and a Way of Life
dostori.d1: “My Constitution… A Balance of the Heart and a Way of Life” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.

desc.h: This book… is not mere talk, but a balance of the heart and a way of life.

desc: This book is not just written pages, nor a collection of educational material and rules set in theoretical frames that minds memorise and actions forget. In essence, this book is the voice of conscience when it wakes, the trust of the soul when it speaks, and a mind that raises the young in the belief that a person is not shaped by the preacher or led by the loud voice, but is built in reverent intention, soundness of mind and love of the truth. The aim of this book is to create in every home a finer human being, in every thoughtful person a fairer scale, and in every father and mother a mirror that helps them see truly, without flattery, leniency or laxity, and without deceiving themselves.

In its pulse it is a book of awakening: it wakes in the reader an idea he had fallen silent about, and a feeling that had almost withered in the crush of false guidance. In its style it is a book of companionship: it takes you by the hand, does not throw you into the depths of theory or tire you with office classifications, but talks to you as a father talks to his child, with love, affection and a resolve for good.

In every chapter there is a meaning that seeks to straighten what has gone crooked, to set in order what has lost its balance, and to give back to upbringing its pure meaning, where a person is raised to think, to feel, and to raise himself by worth, not by appearance, not by loudness, not by looks.

It is a book that understands the child before judging him, and sees the young person as he is, not as we wish him to be; then it speaks to the maturity in him with patience, plants manhood in him with knowledge, and strengthens his inner growth with values, not with orders.

What sets this book apart is that it does not offer a solution and move on; it builds in you a maturity that makes you the maker of the solution. That is why you will find in it much stillness and reflection, and little noise and abruptness. It is for those who want to understand, not for those who want to convince themselves quickly.

As I wrote each sentence of it, I felt it came not from a pen but from a conscience that fears for people and wishes them good in their souls before their lives, that sees in every child a man who deserves to be raised in purity, and in every father a mission that must be safeguarded.

By God, this is a book to read for ourselves before we offer it to others, to read with honest eyes and a heart that wants the ending to be noble. If you come to it with love, it will return you to yourself pure; and if you read it with intention, it will pour on you more insight than a hundred lessons can tell.
God is behind every purpose; in Him is our reliance and our hope, and to Him every good is raised.
This book casts its seed into the heart and moves on, and it is left to you to water it with thought and action, and to make it bear fruit in the world as a mark that stands and bears witness.

We did not come to decree what must be, nor to close the doors of understanding with words. This book was a voice calling in a time of much clamour, and a constitution that addresses the conscience, not authority, hoping in every line to grow in a person something of nobility, something of purity, and something of the strength that is neither sold nor bought.

We wrote to educate, and to light a point of light in the heart of every child, every father and every mother, and in every soul that believes upbringing is an act of immortality, and that the message remains even when its bearer is gone.
And if this book has an end, its constitution hangs in the consciences. We have written its principles in the ink of the heart, and it is left to you to complete it with good deeds.
Whoever raises his child to nobility has written a chapter.
Whoever purifies his intention in giving has completed the lines.
And whoever comes out of this book having kept value in its rightful place is the last author.
So walk by a constitution that does not boast, does not seek fame, does not argue and does not shout, but builds, gives, is sometimes silent, and endures.

kalimat-ahd-wa-rayat-qurb.title: A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness
kalimat-ahd-wa-rayat-qurb.d1: “A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
desc: This book was not born of a passing moment, nor is it the trace of a thought that crossed the heart and went its way. It is the essence of what remains when the noise has gone, the cream of what settles when the excess falls away, and the best of what weighs in the soul after the days have passed over it as clouds pass over mountains: touching them without uprooting them, passing over them without moving them. This book was not written to be a line recited, but to be a scale one returns to; not to be a voice that is heard, but to be a truth that is known, a criterion before which claims are exposed and inner secrets are laid bare. I wrote it certain that books are not sheets of paper gathered together but positions built; not phrases woven but scales set up; not lines packed together but meanings that are tested, carried and kept.

There is not a word in it without a long look behind it, an experience that taught, a trial that refined, and a silence that spoke until it overflowed onto the tongue as eloquence. I have seen people of many kinds; I have heard promises that fill gatherings but never fill real positions; and I have witnessed enough changing of colours to know that the truth needs no ornament, and that falsehood, however much it glitters, remains one-eyed in the eye of insight. So I had no choice but to write: not to please the ear but to wake awareness, not to beautify a meaning but to reveal its face as it is — stern when sternness is needed, gentle when the situation calls for gentleness, lofty and unwilling to accept the low, pure and unwilling to accept the murky. This book, in its essence, is an effort to give back to the covenant its dignity after the careless lost it, to nearness its meaning after the affected cheapened it, and to the word its gravity after it was scattered by those who say much and do little.

In this book I did not want to talk to people about loyalty from a distance, but to bring them into its sanctuary, so that they could see how beautiful it is and how heavy. Loyalty is not a flower that is smelled and then forgotten; it is a tree that must be watered, tended, protected and shielded from the wind of whim and the assaults of self-interest. A covenant is not a sound that leaves the lips; it is a boundary set up in the soul that either raises it or exposes it, for a person may be handsome in his words and then worthless in his stand, and his voice may rise with a promise and then fall at the first test. How many there are who speak, and how few who live up to what they said: you see their words flowing like torrents while the meanings are barren, their faces smiling while their consciences frown, affection displayed while love is absent, and nearness present on the tongue but absent from the heart. That is why I did not write to flatter, nor compose to placate; I did not give the phrase authority over the truth, but gave the truth authority over the phrase. When the wording was narrow, the meaning widened; and when ornament and honesty competed, I chose honesty, even if it came rough to the touch, for roughness in the truth is nobler than the smoothness of falsehood, and clarity, even when it hurts, is more generous than fog, even when it charms. My concern was not that the reader should leave this book merely admiring it, but that he should leave it alert, thoughtful, examining himself: does he carry the name of the covenant, or its substance? Does he raise the banner of nearness sincerely, or use it as a screen? Is he good at naming values, or good at living by them? If he stops with himself in this way, the book has reached its aim, the word has arrived at its place, and the meaning has found its home in the heart and in insight.

As I worked on building this book, I came to believe that true writing does not grow in the soil of haste, nor bloom in the air of affectation; it comes from contemplation mixed with hardship, reflection joined to experience, and patience with meaning until its pure part separates from its dregs and its essence stands out from its impurities. I did not write these pages from the position of a spectator but from inside the battle. I saw how the word rises in one mouth and falls in one hand, how a promise shines in a gathering and then fades at the first test, and how some souls remain lofty, not because they make many claims but because they make few and keep faith much, and not because they are good at presenting themselves but because they are good at carrying their meaning.

Hence this manner of expression: it is not content to move over the surface of meaning but seeks its depth; it is not satisfied with touching the outside but goes beneath it to reach the root. That is why you will find in this book a tone that resembles a scale, which does not lean with desire or tilt with inclination; that resembles a mirror, which does not beautify features but shows them as they are; and that resembles fire, which warms whoever approaches it honestly and burns whoever enters upon it with deceit. What I hope for this book is that it will not be just a work read and then put away, but an awareness that accompanies the reader, a question that pursues him, and a light that remains in the memory after many of the lights of passing noise have gone out; that it will be a light in the reader’s hand guiding him to himself, not an ornament whose glitter he admires and then forgets. In bringing this book to the reader, I am not handing him a text only: I am entrusting him with a trust of meaning, placing a scale in his hands, and inviting him — with a calm that has no weakness in it and a firmness that has no harshness — to enter this station with me as one who wants to know, not as one who merely wants to pass through. For me, “A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness” is not a title placed on a cover, but a vision of the human being who wants to stand higher, live more uprightly and keep a purer heart.

They are a call for the word to regain its weight, nearness its sanctity, loyalty its role as a measure and honesty its authority; a call for a person not to remain a prisoner of what is said about him, but to be the child of what he stands firm on. If the reader finds in these pages something that helps him see himself more clearly, weigh his positions more fairly, carry his covenant more seriously and raise the banner of his nearness more sincerely, then that is what I sought and aimed for. And if the author has one last hope after finishing his work, it is that his book should remain after him as a witness — not only to his skill with words, but to his devotion to the meaning he believed in, and which he wished to remain among people as a light, not a fire; guidance, not whim; a scale, not a bias; a lasting trace, not a fading one; truth, not falsehood; justice, not injustice; remembrance, not forgetting.

If I have made the covenant the title of this book and nearness its banner, it is because I know that people in our time do not need more words so much as they need the return of the scale. There are many now who are good at naming meanings but not at carrying them, skilled at the craft of display but not at the craft of steadfastness; they raise a banner of affection that fades at the first trial, and talk at length about loyalty that vanishes at the slightest cost. How badly our age needs a person in whose hand the word weighs heavy, who does not release it without knowing it will come back to him as a question or a judgement; a heart that, when it draws near, does not draw near to consume but to protect, tend and keep; and a conscience that, once it has made a covenant, no longer allows itself to slacken. For when a covenant enters a noble soul it becomes a sovereign there, not a visitor; and when it settles in a pure heart it becomes a trust, not an ornament; a responsibility, not a claim. That is why my writing does not look for space on paper but for a place in awareness; it does not seek quick admiration but a lasting effect; and it does not want the reader to say, “How beautiful these words are,” but to stop afterwards and say, “How heavy this meaning is for one who is not sincere, and how high it raises one who stands firm by it.” Among the greatest things life has taught me is that the great meanings are not revealed in days of ease as they are in days of hardship, and are not known in hours of contentment as they are in hours of trial. How many shining faces went dark at the first wind; how many names that resounded in gatherings had no voice and no trace in times of hardship; and how many hearts, little mentioned in public but great in the scale of loyalty, are not known in the crowd but are known when people scatter, do not appear when the way is wide but appear when the roads narrow and excuses run out. That is why I did not make this book a praise of values from the outside, but an entry into their test. Talking about loyalty is easy, but carrying it is hard; praising honesty is simple, but standing firm on it is hard; raising the banner of nearness in words is effortless, but keeping it from falling when the days grow tiring is something only a person can do whose inner self is wider than his desires, firmer than his interests and nobler than the impulse of the moment.

I believe that a person sees the truth of himself only when he finds himself between two things: between what he desires and what he ought to do, and between what brings him quick gain and what remains for him in the long run. Here people show what they are made of: are there among them those who carry the meaning and rise with it, or those who ask the meaning to serve their weakness and fall with it? I did not write this book to pick a quarrel with anyone, nor to open a door of reproach against any particular person. I wrote it because I saw that meaning itself deserves to be defended, that value itself deserves a witness in words, and that the human being deserves to be called to a station higher than changeability, consumption and evasion. How badly meanings are lost when they are left to those who merely claim them; how quickly the word is cheapened when it is carried by one who cannot weigh it; and how ugly it is when frivolity is called gentleness, inconstancy wisdom, self-interest affection and slackness broad-mindedness. That is why I gave this book a voice that joins tenderness with resolve and walks between light and fire. It is not harsh in order to hurt, nor soft in order to deceive; it seeks to be, in its place, like a sword when cutting is needed, like water when cleansing is needed, and like light when revealing is needed. I do not think books last only because their wording is fine; they last when they join to fine wording sincerity of purpose, to beautiful construction nobility of aim, and to strength of expression a noble goal. If this book is destined to last, it will not be only because it wrote well, but because it tried to be faithful to a great meaning in an age when meanings have grown light for many people.

In these words I do not claim to have grasped the meaning from every side. The highest meanings are wider than pages can contain and more lasting than any single book can exhaust. But I hope I have pointed to their door, raised a sign for them, and left on the road to them something that guides the traveller without taking over his journey. For me, “A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness” are not letters arranged to please the eye, but a meaning that should rise in a person until it becomes part of his structure, a light that should join his conscience until it becomes part of his insight, and a scale that should stand in his conduct until it becomes part of his life.

If the reader finds in these pages something that helps him see himself more truly, weigh his positions more fairly, carry his covenant more seriously and raise the banner of his nearness more purely, then the purpose has been achieved and the word has been put in its place.

And if the author, having finished his book, has a hope to rest in, it is that this work should remain after him as a witness — not only to his skill, but to his devotion to the meaning he believed in, which he wished to remain among people as a light that does not fade, a guidance that does not stray, a scale that does not tilt, and a trace that points to the sincerity of its author before it points to his ability. When the author finishes setting out what he has, he does not finish with his meaning, for a living meaning does not stop at the end of the line; it rises again in the soul, the mind and the conscience. This afterword is not a return to what has been said, nor a repetition of what has passed; it is meaning travelling to its furthest reach, where speech no longer remains speech but becomes an awareness taking shape, a scale finding its balance, and a stand by which a person distinguishes himself from his own self before he distinguishes himself from others. When I named my book “A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness”, I did not want it to stop at the limits of the name, but to reach an essence too large for names and wide enough for real positions. A covenant is not a meaning called up for its pleasant sound; it is something on which obligations are built, which weighs on people’s necks, and by which a person rises or falls in rank. And nearness is not merely closeness that looks good on the outside; it is a bond that, when it is true, turns into tranquillity in the heart and steadfastness in hardship, and into a banner that is raised not by the beauty of its colours but by the sincerity of those who stand firm beneath it. That is why this book continues beyond the author’s word: some meanings begin to be expressed only when people think the expression is complete, and reveal their depths only when the listener imagines there is nothing more to say. As I turned over the course of human life with covenant and nearness, it became clear to me that the great problem is not people’s ignorance of meanings but how lightly those meanings weigh in many souls. They know loyalty with their tongues but do not keep it in their positions; they praise honesty in their speeches but are uncomfortable with it when it becomes a burden on them; they raise nearness as a slogan but cannot keep it when the road is long, the load heavy and circumstances hard.

Hence the tragedy lies not in the absence of names but in the erosion of essences; not in poverty of the tongue but in poverty of the heart; not in a shortage of those who speak but in the rarity of those who stand firm. When I say “a word of covenant”, I mean a word that, once spoken, is no longer a sound in the air but a boundary in the conscience. And when I say “a banner of nearness”, I mean a nearness that is not cut off when contact is cut, nor withers when the season cools, but remains in the depths of the soul as a root remains in the earth: not all of it is seen, but its effect is known in steadfastness and endurance. What most exposes falsehood here is that many people are good at entering into meanings but not at remaining in them: they know how affection begins but not the sanctity of keeping it up; they are skilled at dazzling the moment but not at carrying year after year with the same face of sincerity. I believe the author’s role is not complete just because he writes what he has; it is complete when he sets his reader before himself, stripped bare, leaving him no escape into embellishment and no refuge in loose interpretation.

This is what I wanted for this book: that in the hands of its reader it should be not a pillow on which he rests his thinking, but a scale to which he returns; not a window through which he looks at others, but a mirror in which he looks at himself; not jewellery for taste, but a file for the excesses that have clung to the conscience. And because I know that an author may become enchanted by the splendour of his own words and forget their essence, I tried here to make them servants of the meaning, not its masters. When beautiful construction and nobility of purpose competed, I gave precedence to nobility of purpose; and when the truth needed a word less smooth and more honest, I preferred it to everything else. Writing that gives up its right to reveal in order to keep a pleasing effect is like a creature with a beautiful face and a corrupt heart. Writing that does justice to its meaning is the writing that lasts, because it draws its life not only from the freshness of its words but from the strength of what it carries and the truth of what it testifies to.

Perhaps this is the secret of why some texts drift away like the wind and others stay like mountains: the first were said to impress, the second were written to establish a meaning, carry a truth and leave among people an effect that is renewed every time they return to them.

I do not want this afterword to be a conclusion that closes the door, but a key that opens what comes after it, for a meaning that stops at the book is an incomplete meaning, while the meaning that goes out with the reader into his life is the one that deserves to last. If I have said what I said about the covenant, the aim is not that the listener should admire it, but that he should ask himself in every situation: am I one of the people of the word when it becomes heavy? And if I have raised the standing of nearness, the aim is not that it should please the taste, but that it should become a constant question in the soul: do I carry the banner of my nearness sincerely, or do I wear it as an ornament to show people what I do not practise within myself? So I hope that this book, with what it contains and what extends from it, will be a point of return to the origin after much scattering, a point of waking after long habit, and a point of rising after long neglect. And if I may wish for anything after all this, my wish is that these words should not pass over hearts as a shadow passes, but enter them as light enters: revealing without shaming, raising up without overpowering, inviting without evading. If some of that comes to pass, then “A Word of Covenant and a Banner of Nearness” will have achieved something of what it was made for: to be wakefulness in souls, a scale in consciences, a proof in positions, and a trace in the days that does not vanish.

Meaning does not stop at the limit of what has been said; it extends through the days as a river extends beyond its source, widening at times and narrowing at others, but never ceasing as long as there is water flowing in it. So too this meaning: it is not content to be read but asks to be lived; it is not satisfied with being kept in memory but wants to dwell in action. When the reader leaves the page, the page begins to open onto him; when he finishes reading, the reviewing begins; and when he thinks he has understood, it is revealed to him that the meaning holds remnants that are grasped only with patience and time. Here the positions change: the person is no longer looking at the meaning but is being looked at through it; the covenant is no longer what is mentioned but what is tested; nearness is no longer what is said but what is carried. From here another road opens whose landmarks are not seen at first glance but appear as one walks, as the weight of illusion grows lighter in souls and the claim of truth grows heavier; words turn into positions and meanings into burdens to be carried, not echoes to be repeated. Not everyone who sets out arrives, and not everyone who sees stands firm: some fade at the first fatigue, and some grow stronger at the first test; and between a fading that withers and a strengthening that lasts, it becomes clear who carries the meaning and who carries only its name.

In this extension the scales are overturned in a way that does not return things to what they were, but raises them to what they ought to be. Speech has authority only to the extent that action supports it, and an image has splendour only to the extent that its substance upholds it. There it becomes known who builds and who decorates, who makes firm and who merely polishes; there ornament falls and truth remains, a voice fades and a trace rises. Either one makes meaning the servant of his desires and becomes light, or he makes himself the servant of meaning and becomes weighty and rises; and between a lightness that loses and a weight that sustains, people are distinguished not by what they say but by what they stand firm on. How great is the difference between one who hurries and loses his goal, and one who guards his steps well and reaches it; for the road does not keep the traveller — it is the traveller who keeps the road or loses it. Here meaning is completed not by ending but by enduring: it is not a conclusion folded away but a trace that remains, not a voice that fades but a presence that is renewed, until it becomes a landmark in the days, a criterion in positions, and something in souls that does not fade.

fi-rihab-al-hurriya.title: In the Realm of Freedom
fi-rihab-al-hurriya.sub: An Anthem of Setting Out, a Declaration of Beginning
fi-rihab-al-hurriya.d1: “In the Realm of Freedom” is a book by Dr. Yousef Ahmad Al-Maiari, published by Al-Maktaba Al-Asriyya in Sidon, Lebanon.
desc: As I bid farewell to the pages of this book, I feel that I am not merely folding paper; I am folding with it a long journey into the depths of meaning and the essence of values. These words were never ink on paper: they were a heartbeat in a chest, a flame on a road, and a covenant that wishes to stay with the generations. And the greatest thing we wanted to establish here is that true freedom is not a slogan to be raised or a word to be repeated; it is a responsibility to be guarded, and a pledge carried on the shoulder of every generation.

True freedom, my friend, is for a person to be honest with himself, pure in heart, faithful in deed and brave in his stand. It is not a gift that is handed out, nor spoils to be divided; it is a noble soul raised on dignity, love and justice. How fine it is to raise our sons to know that freedom is the safeguarding of dignity, and to teach our daughters that freedom is the shelter of values and the keeping of the self. Freedom, in its essence, is not a departure from morals; it is the return of morals to their highest station.

Great nations, my friend, are not measured by the size of their armies or the number of their palaces, but by the free hearts and chaste souls they raise. When the son grows up on dignity and the daughter is raised on virtue, the nation becomes like a building that no age can bring down and no storm can shake. How could it be otherwise, when true freedom means that the homeland is one large family, in which the body is protected, values are preserved, and offspring are cared for through marriage, responsibility and good character?

How splendid it is to realise that true freedom is the key to progress, the scale of justice and the dawn of dignity. It is what frees the mind to create, the heart to love, the hand to build and the tongue to speak the truth. True freedom is for us to be ourselves, not borrowed images or counterfeit voices. It is to tell the age plainly what we believe, and to be a clear page in the book of history.

I urge the reader, as he closes the pages of this book, to make true freedom a covenant he carries in his heart, a bequest he hands down to his children, and a key with which he opens the doors of tomorrow. True freedom is to raise generations who believe in justice, walk by values and lift the banner of love. And how eloquent it would be if the end of this book were the beginning of a new bequest, living in every sincere heart.

I know that the pen may run dry and the paper may be folded away, but true freedom neither dries up nor folds away. It is the pulse of nations, the light of the road and the covenant of tomorrow. History will record that a nation that believed in it endured, that a people who carried it rose, and that a book that called for it was a voice echoing in the hearts of the generations. If the book has ended, the meaning has not; and if the words have come to rest on paper, they go on beating in every free heart. So keep this covenant, and make true freedom forever the key to your lives: it is our bequest to you, and our voice after the pen falls silent.

A book, at the end of its road, is nothing but a testimony of presence in an age that wants meanings to wither and values to shrink until they become a faded shadow. Here there is no room for embellishment and no escape for evasion: either a freedom that brings forth an upright human being, or a falsehood that wraps decline in soft words and drives the fall forward dressed as progress. Nations do not collapse suddenly; they drift little by little until they find themselves without a trace, without a direction and without meaning.
